assessment: The author abstract reports 75 participants with Parkinson disease and 65 matched controls, scale alpha 0.85 and area under the ROC curve 0.704 with a floor effect. Author-hosted instruments separate drooling and swallowing. Original result tables remain unavailable.

Among 76 referred participants, three had Parkinson disease. The aggregate outcome measures laryngeal penetration using standardized test boluses under a posture comparison. No Parkinson-specific estimate or drooling measure.
The scoping review and supplement report heterogeneous findings across separate measures of oral dryness, salivary flow and drooling. No graded fig effect.

Among 203 retrospective charts, the index and post-index worsening rates were 7% and 6% for sialorrhea and 2% and 9% for dysphagia. Four separately coded sialorrhea adverse events were reported. No paired severity or measured fig exposure.

The study reports 41 participants with Parkinson disease, 31 controls and correlation 0.848 with MDS-UPDRS item II.2. The evidence validates a scale with no dietary intervention or raw-fig comparison.

A 111-person online survey separately assessed dry mouth and drooling. Unadjusted drooling estimates for gum, candies and coffee have intervals spanning zero. The adjusted gum result concerns dry mouth and there is no raw-fig measure.
